newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan stocks end flat, cheap stocks dominate.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan stocks end flat, cheap stocks dominate.

text.p: Stocks closed mostly unchanged after low priced shares dominated trading on Friday, with many investors forced to the sidelines by the market's poor liquidity, brokers said.
The Colombo Stock Exchange all share index closed 0.02 points lower at 559.23. Hatton National Bank fell five rupees to 195 and Abans Electrical two to 55.

"There is buying interest among stocks with attractive profit levels, but the problem is to source shares," said a trader at brokerage Lanka Secureities. Sellers have retreated to the sidelines, awaiting further rises in the index, he said.
Trading in late session was half-hearted with many investors and brokers leaving the market early for this afternoon's cricket match between Australia and Sri Lanka, brokers said.
"Many broking offices have now been left with a skeleton staff, as seniors have rushed off to the stadium or to watch the match on television," one said.

Turnover was 23.03 million rupees, with 2.1 million shares changing hands. Volume was supported by 15,000 Blue Diamonds Jewellery shares, which ended unchanged at 12.75 rupees, and 600,000 Dockyard, which fell 0.25 cents to 10.50.
